acceptance: Add exactly the additive CMP-3 migration (Supplier TIN fields: tinType, tinEncrypted, tinLast4, legalName, w9ReceivedOn, w9FileUrl, backupWithholding) with no changes to existing rows; the model stays covered by backup and schema health.

A supplier's TIN is encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM via field-crypto), only its last 4 are ever shown, and the full TIN never appears in logs, audits, prepared filing data beyond the filing outputs themselves, or exports other than the IRIS CSV and recipient copies the owner approves.

The W-9 request uses the existing supplier email path and a one-time upload page at /w9/{token}: rate limited, single use, 14-day expiry, accepting the IRS W-9 PDF upload or a typed form that produces a filled W-9 PDF stored in the private compliance/w9/ area.
Paying a 1099-marked supplier with no W-9 on file raises a To do naming the 24% backup-withholding rule (rate read via ruleAsOf), and the warning clears once the W-9 is recorded.

1099 preparation for a payment year computes per-supplier source-confirmed amounts from the books on the same basis as the existing 1099 review query, excludes card-paid amounts (non-payment-source accounts), splits NEC vs MISC by the expense category's ledger-account box mapping, and compares against the dated threshold ruleAsOf(us.1099.threshold).

Outputs: the IRIS Taxpayer Portal CSV matches the vendored IRS template header exactly and holds at most 100 rows per file; recipient Copy B PDFs are filled from the vendored official 1099-NEC/MISC PDFs through the hash-manifest form engine; both are produced only inside the CMP-1 prepare flow, so the owner's approval binds them by the prepared hash.

The IRIS A2A client is built behind IRIS_A2A_ENABLED (off) with an owner checklist row for the A2A TCC; its request building is tested against Pub 5718 fixtures with no network in tests, and the portal CSV path is the live route until the switch is on.

The Form 8300 detector: recording a customer cash payment (method CASH) that alone or with related cash payments from the same customer within 12 months exceeds $10,000 creates the fed.8300 filing (due 15 days after the triggering payment) and its To do surfaces through COMPLIANCE_DUE.

Tests named by the card pass: tests/w9-integration.test.ts and tests/1099-prep-integration.test.ts, plus the IRIS CSV header test and the 8300 detector test; the Compliance screen browser spec still passes with axe.
invariants: Nothing is filed with the IRS without the owner's Approve on the exact prepared numbers (CMP-1 preparedHash binding); the A2A switch stays off until Chris has the TCC and turns it on.
Vendor TINs are encrypted at rest, shown only as last 4, decrypted only inside filing preparation and the W-9 record itself, and never logged or audited in full.
Money stays integer cents; times are stored UTC and shown America/Denver; writes lock the row first and re-check the actor inside the transaction.
Card-paid vendor amounts are never in 1099-NEC/MISC totals (the card company reports them on 1099-K); unclassified expense categories are surfaced for a decision, never silently guessed into a box.
No invented rates, dates or legal answers: the Colorado 1099 copy question and any unconfirmed rule become a Decisions question with a careful starting value.
next: Full tests, CI, review, merge; then CMP-2 (income tax helpers) on the CMP-1/CMP-3 foundation.
outcome: 1099 season works end to end: suppliers get a W-9 request with a one-time upload page and their TINs are stored encrypted; paying a 1099 vendor without a W-9 raises the backup-withholding To do; the app prepares each year's 1099-NEC/MISC amounts from the books (card payments excluded, threshold from the dated rule), produces the IRIS portal CSV (at most 100 rows, exact IRS header) and filled recipient copies under the owner's hash-bound approval; the A2A direct-filing client exists behind its switch; and a cash payment over $10,000 triggers the Form 8300 filing and To do.

The existing source-confirmed 1099 review query and its dated-threshold read — preparation builds on the same basis so the review and the filing can never disagree.
